expectations.text: The skill recognizes this as an underspecified request (cannot achieve 95% confidence from 2 words)
expectations.evidence: Transcript: 'Assessment: Confidence is extremely low — approximately 10-15%.' and 'Result: 0 of 6 criteria met. Confidence: ~10%'

expectations.text: The first elicitation round asks about problem statement, scope, and what 'dark mode' means in context
expectations.evidence: Transcript Round 1 includes: 'What application/UI is this dark mode for?', 'What problem does dark mode solve?', 'What is explicitly IN scope?'

expectations.text: Questions cover at least 3 of these dimensions: scope boundaries, user-facing behavior, integration points, persistence strategy, existing theming infrastructure
expectations.evidence: Transcript covers all 5: Scope Boundaries (Q3-4), User-Facing Behavior (Q7-9), Integration Points (Q12-13), Persistence Strategy (Q8), Existing Theming (Q12,17). Also covers edge cases, constraints, and accessibility.

expectations.text: The skill does NOT proceed to Phase 2 without at least one round of user clarification
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 7: 'The skill explicitly states: Only proceed to Phase 2 when confidence >= 95% OR user explicitly says proceed. At ~10% confidence, proceeding would be reckless. The team lead would NOT proceed.'

expectations.text: The skill uses AskUserQuestion (not just text output) to collect user input
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 4: 'Since confidence < 95%, the skill mandates using AskUserQuestion to elicit missing details.'

expectations.text: After user responds, the skill re-assesses confidence before deciding whether to ask more questions
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 5: 'Confidence Re-assessment (Hypothetical)' — estimates ~50-65% after Round 1, plans Round 2 targeting remaining gaps, and Round 3 for final confirmation

suggestions.reason: The agent produced 17 questions in Round 1. While thorough, this is overwhelming for a user. The graduated elicitation improvement (added in iteration 2) should reduce this to 8-15 for low-confidence requests, prioritizing the most critical unknowns first.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions passed. The skill correctly identified extreme underspecification and refused to proceed. Question quality was high but quantity was too large — addressed in skill improvements.
